html:
A Byzantine monk and theologian, one of the deepest thinkers of the Greek church. According to his Greek biography he was a senior official under the emperor Heraclius before he became a monk.

He became the leading opponent of Monothelitism, the idea that Christ had only one will, which the emperors promoted to win over Christians who rejected Chalcedon. Maximus argued that if Christ was fully human, he must have a human will as well as a divine one. He took this fight to Africa and to Rome, where Pope Martin I's Lateran Council condemned Monothelitism in 649.

The emperor Constans II had him arrested and put on trial. He refused to give in. In 662 his tongue and right hand were cut off so that he could not speak or write against the emperor, and he died in exile in Lazica, in today's Georgia. The Third Council of Constantinople in 680 and 681 upheld his view. His writings blend Christian faith with ideas from Neoplatonism.
sum: A Byzantine monk and theologian, one of the deepest thinkers of the Greek church. According to his Greek biography he was a senior official under the emperor Heraclius before he became a monk.
